issue.title: Bound oversized inline notification action payloads
issue.description: PROPOSED BY sase-zn.3 note 1 during ACE typing-lag work. Independent landing audit at primary e498ce822 on 2026-09-12 found 1,585 live notification rows occupying 12,065,024 bytes; JSON-encoded action_data p95 9,195 bytes and max 1,944,239 bytes. Large inline action payloads survive dismissed-row compaction and still impose parsing, serialization, and memory cost whenever the store changes. Design durable references or another bounded representation for bulky payloads while preserving actions, replay, archived notification reads, and existing producer/consumer contracts. This predates sase-zn and its plan expressly defers payload redesign. Do not fold the sase-zn.3 snapshot token race into this task: that defect remains parent-epic work. Size large because the cross-producer storage/compatibility design needs planning. Searched bug and feature tasks across all statuses, swept all recent tasks, and inspected active epics; no same-remedy task or causally responsible active epic found.

task_type_fields.impact: Every changed-store read reparses bulky inline data even after dismissed-history compaction, increasing refresh cost and retained memory.
task_type_fields.repro: On athena, count and size rows in ~/.sase/notifications/notifications.jsonl and JSON-encode each action_data to measure its bytes; the landing audit records a 1,944,239-byte maximum and 12,065,024-byte active file. No payload content needs to be printed.
